chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) had judged regarding a woman who gifted her maid to her husband, so he fell upon her. So the slave girl became pregnant and the woman denied that she had gifted her to him, and she said, 'She is my servant'. So when she feared that the Penalty (Hadd) would be established upon the man, she confessed that she had gifted her to him.
So when she has accepted having gifted, she should be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) due to her having slandered her husband.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.قَذْف: Qadhf (slander, specifically accusing a free Muslim of adultery)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a woman who gifts her slave to her husband and then denies it to avoid his punishment?
ai.summary: This case from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the legal principle of 'Qadhf' (slander) applied to a free woman accusing her husband of illicit relations with her slave. The ruling highlights the strategic denial and subsequent confession to avoid the husband's punishment, ultimately resulting in the woman receiving the Hadd penalty for slander, demonstrating the precise application of evidentiary standards in Shia jurisprudence.
